The major will allow participants to explore the food chain, from farm to plate to waste and back, emphasizing sustainability, impacts on human health, and resilience from economic, environmental, and societal viewpoints.

Core values of this interdisciplinary program that distinguish it from more traditional agriculture programs include an emphasis on the intrinsic value of heterogeneous scales of production (from small farms that sell directly to consumers to large scale producers), preserving local food cultures and biodiversity while understanding the way other cultures produce and use food (from local to global), using an ecosystem-based approach to agriculture (also integrating the contributions of aquaculture and fisheries), and the greening of urban landscapes.
By the time of degree completion students will be uniquely poised to enter the workforce in the growing field of sustainable food systems or pursue management (through governmental and non- governmental agencies) and graduate education/research opportunities addressing the challenges of securing access to safe and affordable food for a growing population.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) in multiple fields toward an undergraduate degree.

It is well-suited for students whose career goals call for training in more than one discipline or who want a breadth of knowledge in several fields rather than a depth of knowledge in a single discipline.
With this degree, one can be even more directly educated with regard to several, specific, job-relevant studies.
This interdisciplinary “three-minor’ major also may work well for students who do not want to limit their career options by majoring in just one area of study.
For the purposes of this proposal, the word “minor" is used to refer to coursework associated with recognized areas of study (as minors) at the University of Rhode Island.
Specifically, students will complete an application that proposes one thematic or topical concentration made up of three (3) recognized minor areas of study that will not be restricted

to conventional departmental or unit boundaries.
The application must include a statement of rationale for the combination of areas of study.
The application then must be reviewed and approved by the Director of School of Professional and Continuing Studies (or designee).
Students seeking this program must declare it as their major in the same manner, and at the same time,that other URI students declare a major.
It is important to note that, through the completion of this program, students will not receive minors in the three areas of study, rather the integrated coursework will be used to fulfill the requirements of the interdisciplinary major.
Upon completion of the program, the student's approved interdisciplinary concentration will be noted on the university transcript.
Moreover, the Learner Designed major provides an opportunity to develop and pursue a course of study centered on a unifying theme, problem, or issue.
Students earning a degree in Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies, Learner Designed major will: · Possess an interdisciplinary perspective by integrating knowledge and skills from three areas of study.

Communicate meaningful connections effectively across disciplinary boundaries.
The Learner Designed major will include: (a) URI General Education Requirements; (b) Minor Area of Study 1 (18- 24 credits), Minor Area of Study 2 (18 -24 credits), and Minor Area of Study 3 (18 -24 credits); (c) BIS 100, 399, ITR 302, 304; and, (d) elective courses totaling 120 credit hours.
The capstone experience (BIS 399) provides a structure that enables the student to integrate knowledge and skills from coursework and related experiences with a research project.
The project must be designed so that it allows the student to demonstrate the integration of subject matter, theory, and practice.
Students are required to meet with the Director of School of Professional & Continuing Studies (or designee) to plan a project proposal.
The Learner Designed major will provide students with a well-rounded education in multiple academic disciplines, allowing them to gain skills employers will find desirable, including critical thinking, communication and creative problem-solving.
Employers appreciate applicants with diverse backgrounds and the ability to integrate multiple viewpoints.
